title: Tech Note: An Approach to Preferences
author: Timothy Aaron Penner, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D DOM XML commands (in-memory XML preferences store)
Custom XML preferences file format with theme support

historical_commentary.text: This note proposed a themed, XML-file-based preferences engine built on 4D's DOM commands as an alternative to storing application settings inside 4D's data engine — a sensible pattern at the time given the tooling available. The core idea (external, human-editable, easily copyable preference storage) remains sound today, but current 4D applications more commonly use 4D's native JSON object support (JSON Parse/Stringify, the dot/bracket object syntax) rather than DOM-based XML for this kind of key-value configuration store, since JSON is simpler to read/write and integrates naturally with 4D's object and collection types introduced in later versions.
related_updates: 4D's native JSON support (objects/collections, JSON Parse and JSON Stringify) is now generally preferred over DOM-based XML for lightweight preferences/configuration storage
4D's object (ORDA/entity) storage or a simple JSON file are common modern alternatives to a custom XML preferences component
